stories.title: From biotech to finance, a career pivot
stories.summary: Saurav Petwe, an IIT Kharagpur Biotechnology graduate, has transitioned into financial engineering. Now a student at the Indian School of Business, Petwe previously worked at Deutsche Bank and Credit Suisse. His career path reflects a shift from laboratory research toward data analysis and problem solving in global finance.

stories.title: Texas college updates tech curriculum for AI
stories.summary: Texas State Technical College is updating its cybersecurity and computer networking programs to incorporate artificial intelligence. The school aims to prepare students for an industry where AI tools are increasingly common. Officials suggest that while AI is changing the nature of technical work, it will likely transform jobs rather than

stories.title: Insider Information: College Students Weigh In on AI's Impact on Careers and Coursework - U.S. News & World Report
Students shift toward practical careers
stories.summary: Enrolments in construction courses at Bishop Burton College have risen 21 percent this year, marking four consecutive years of growth. Students cited the value of practical skills in an AI-driven economy, with one student noting that AI cannot deliver a lamb.

stories.title: AI Is Changing Jobs, Not Ending Them: What Should Students Study To Stay Employable? - شبكة تواصل الإخبارية
India shifts focus toward computational thinking
stories.summary: Schools are moving away from teaching chatbot prompting toward foundational computational thinking and logical reasoning. Educators argue that training children on specific interfaces is ineffective if the technology becomes obsolete. The goal is to teach students how to process information and question the answers that machines produce.

stories.title: Human skills remain a priority in AI-heavy workplaces
stories.summary: As artificial intelligence becomes standard in most workplaces, employers are increasingly prioritizing human strengths. Data shows that new job responsibilities in AI-exposed roles are twice as likely to require empathy and judgment. Schools are being encouraged to emphasize these non-replicable human skills to prepare students for the economy.

stories.title: Districts struggle to keep CTE programs relevant
stories.summary: The rapid pace of technological change is complicating efforts to align career and technical education with current workplace needs. Industry experts note that even employers are finding it difficult to provide clear guidance on what skills will be required for future readiness in a shifting economy.

stories.title: From food delivery to pilot training
stories.summary: Haizil Jebin, a 29-year-old from Kerala, is pursuing a career as a commercial pilot after working as a food delivery driver. Despite academic setbacks, Jebin completed private pilot training at an academy in the Philippines. He is currently working toward his commercial license to fulfill a childhood ambition.

stories.title: Kota coaching centers see MIT admissions
stories.summary: Kota, a hub for competitive exam preparation, has seen 18 students secure admission to the Massachusetts Institute of Technology over the past nine years. While the city is primarily known for JEE engineering entrance coaching, it is increasingly serving as a pipeline for global university applications.

stories.title: Udaipur student advances to national skating championship
stories.summary: Shambhavi Sunil Kumar Saraswat, a Class 3 student at Maharana Mewar Vidya Mandir, has qualified for the CBSE National Skating Championship. She earned her spot after winning a silver medal in the Quads 1 Lap Road Race at the CBSE West Zone Skating Tournament held in Jaipur.

stories.title: Oriental Mindoro student earns ASMO Grand Slam, bags multiple international academic awards - Philippine Information Age
Armenian team wins six medals at astronomy olympiad
stories.summary: All six members of Armenia's team won medals at the International Open Astronomy Olympiad in Russia. The group secured two gold and four silver medals among 69 participants from 14 countries. The competition was held in the Sirius Federal Territory from November 6 to 14.

stories.title: Armenian students win six medals at astronomy olympiad
stories.summary: Armenia's six-member team secured two gold and four silver medals at the International Open Astronomy Olympiad in Russia. The competition, held from November 6 to 14, included 69 participants from 14 countries. The gold medalists are students from the A. Shahinyan Physics and Mathematics Specialized School in Yerevan.

stories.title: Armenian students win six medals at astronomy olympiad
stories.summary: Armenia's team won two gold and four silver medals at the Open World Astronomy Olympiad in Russia. The event hosted 69 participants from 14 countries. The Ministry of Education, Science, Culture and Sports of Armenia confirmed that all six team members earned medals during the November competition.

stories.title: Bangladesh wins silver in global ranking at Russia's Youth Geography Olympiad - Daily Sun
Bangladesh second in Geography Olympiad, wins five medals - Banglanews24
IIIT-H students build sign language web plugin
stories.summary: Students at IIIT-Hyderabad have developed a browser plugin to translate web content into Indian Sign Language in real time. The tool functions without server-side AI models or specialized hardware. It aims to improve online accessibility for users with hearing impairments by converting text into visual gestures.

stories.title: Bangladesh to field team at 28th int'l robot olympiad in Austria - Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha (BSS)
Philippine-made robotics kits used at Dubai competition
stories.summary: Robolution 2026 brought 249 students from 24 schools to the BITS Pilani campus in Dubai. Most events utilized Philippine-made Erobot kits, developed by Erovoutika. The competition, organized by the manufacturer and the university, allowed students to compete with their own robot designs in three open categories.

stories.title: Bangladesh selects team for International AI Olympiad
stories.summary: The Bangladesh Open Source Network has named four students to represent the country at the third International Artificial Intelligence Olympiad in Vietnam. The competition expects 300 participants from over 40 countries. Team members were selected based on their combined results across three stages of the national competition.

stories.title: International Anatomy Olympiad 2027 to be held in Estonia
stories.summary: The University of Tartu is hosting the International Anatomy Olympiad in August 2027. Teams of three students will represent their universities in the competition, which was first held in 2019. Last year, 60 students from 14 countries participated, with the University of Ljubljana taking the top spot.

stories.title: BNTU students place third at heat power engineering olympiad
stories.summary: A team from the Belarusian National Technical University placed third at the 10th All-Russian Olympiad on heat power engineering. The event, held at Ivanovo State Energy University, featured teams from several technical institutions across Russia. The BNTU team was led by senior lecturer Vera Yanchuk.

stories.title: BNTU hosts national blitz-olympiad in customs affairs
stories.summary: The Belarusian National Technical University hosted the 5th National Blitz-Olympiad in Customs Affairs, featuring teams from five higher education institutions. The dean of the faculty of management technologies addressed the future professionals, noting that such events help students from different regions establish connections.

stories.title: CBSE releases math practice questions for 2027 exams
stories.summary: The CBSE has released 50 multiple-choice questions for the 2027 Class 12 Mathematics board exam. The board describes the subject as one of the most difficult, requiring regular practice of formulas. The materials are designed to align with the latest rationalized NCERT syllabus and competency requirements.

stories.title: CBSE publishes biology sample paper for 2027 board exams
stories.summary: The CBSE has released its Class 12 Biology sample paper and marking scheme for the 2027 examinations. The board says the paper helps students understand the balance between theoretical knowledge and analytical thinking. The materials are available for download on the official academic website.

stories.title: Guidance on identifying children's strengths
stories.summary: Experts suggest parents create supportive environments for children to explore various opportunities and talents. Because future career paths are considered unpredictable, the focus should remain on building foundational skills and a willingness to learn throughout life. Parents are encouraged to help children spot their own strengths.

stories.title: Educator says AI shifts classroom focus to process
stories.summary: A Kelowna educator says teachers are shifting focus from providing correct answers to the process of learning. Because AI can generate answers instantly, teaching methods are changing. The director of innovation at Aberdeen Hall Preparatory School noted that AI is now embedded in everything students do.

stories.title: Students discuss AI concerns during mock interviews
stories.summary: High school seniors in New York participated in mock job interviews with 130 local employers. While students described the experience as positive, many expressed nervousness regarding the role of artificial intelligence in the modern workforce. The event was held at the Watertown International Airport.

stories.title: Students explore AI careers at Red Wing bootcamp
stories.summary: Twenty-three students from 13 schools attended an AI bootcamp in Red Wing to learn about machine learning and computing. The three-Saturday event concluded with students presenting projects developed alongside industry mentors. The program was hosted by local public schools and the Red Wing Ignite Innovation Hub.

stories.title: New casebook surveys developments in AI law
stories.summary: Professor Margot Kaminski has co-authored a new casebook titled Artificial Intelligence Law. Published by Foundation Press, the book covers legal topics including automated decision-making, privacy, and generative AI. It surveys developments in policy through five distinct lenses for students and legal professionals.

stories.title: Winners announced for international finance olympiad
stories.summary: The Turkmen State Institute of Economics and Management announced the results of the III Open International Internet Olympiad in Finance. About 200 students from 11 countries participated, with 121 prize places awarded. Participants had 120 minutes to answer 10 questions in Turkmen, English, or Russian.

stories.title: Bangladesh team earns silver at geography olympiad
stories.summary: The Bangladesh team secured second place globally at the Multinational Youth Geography Olympiad held in Russia. All five team members earned individual medals, including two silver and three bronze. The competition evaluated students on academic knowledge, practical skills, and problem-solving abilities across five days.

stories.title: Armenia wins six medals at astronomy olympiad
stories.summary: Armenia's team won two gold and four silver medals at the International Open Astronomy Olympiad in Russia. The competition brought together 69 contestants from 14 countries. All six Armenian participants, including four students from the Shahinyan Physics and Mathematics Specialised School, secured medals.

stories.title: Turkmenistan students win medals at math competition
stories.summary: Students from Magtymguly Turkmen State University won five medals at the International Student Team Competition in Mathematics in Poland. The university secured one gold and three bronze medals in individual categories, plus a bronze medal in the team competition. The event was organized by the University of Silesia.

stories.title: UK universities warn students of impersonation scams
stories.summary: The University of Nottingham has warned international students to treat unprompted contact with scepticism. Scammers are reportedly impersonating police and embassy officials to claim students are involved in crimes like money laundering, demanding payment to avoid arrest or deportation. Urgency is a common feature of the approach.

stories.title: Girls On Campus offers $1,500 scholarship for leadership
stories.summary: Girls On Campus is accepting applications for its $1,500 She Leads Scholarship for students planning to attend US colleges in fall 2027. The programme prioritises everyday leadership and initiative over academic awards or major achievements. It aims to support students committed to making a positive difference in their communities.

stories.title: American Open University announces N760m scholarship scheme
stories.summary: American Open University Nigeria and the American College of Technology are launching the O’GIFTS Scholarship. The scheme provides N760 million in tuition support for 500 Ogbomoso students over five years. It is named in honour of the Soun of Ogbomosoland and will be launched virtually on November 24.

stories.title: Seven students receive Claude McKay Scholarship Awards
stories.summary: The Jamaica Association of Maryland awarded the 2026 Claude McKay Scholarship to seven students of Jamaican heritage. The recipients were honoured at the association’s 38th anniversary banquet in Randallstown, Maryland. The funds are intended to assist the students in furthering their studies at their respective institutions.

stories.title: Students compete for secondary school scholarship
stories.summary: Abraham Seed Private School International has invited 2,000 students to sit for its 2026/2027 scholarship examination. The school will select 200 winners for the award. The programme has run for over 10 years as part of the school’s corporate social responsibility initiative to assist students with examination fees.

stories.title: MTSU concludes recruitment tour with $500,000 in scholarships
stories.summary: Middle Tennessee State University has finished its 2026 True Blue Tour after 10 stops across Tennessee and Alabama. President Sidney A. McPhee led the recruitment effort, which awarded more than $500,000 in scholarships to prospective students. The tour showcased the university’s 300 available undergraduate and graduate degree programmes.

stories.title: OHL announces 2026 David Branch Leadership Scholarship recipients
stories.summary: The Ontario Hockey League and Special Olympics Ontario have named four students as the 2026 recipients of the David Branch Leadership Scholarship. Each student will receive $5,000 for post-secondary education. The scholarship honours the late OHL commissioner and is now in its second year of operation.

stories.title: UGC NET December 2026 exam schedule released
stories.summary: The University Grants Commission has released the subject-wise schedule for the December 2026 NET examinations. Tests are set to begin on December 14 and continue through December 16. Candidates can check the official website for specific shift timings and city intimation details for their respective subjects.

stories.title: Chhattisgarh Board releases 2027 exam timetable
stories.summary: The Chhattisgarh Board of Secondary Education has published the 2027 timetable for Class 10 and 12 examinations. Class 10 exams are scheduled to run from March 13 to April 5. The papers will be held in a single daily shift from 9 am to 12.15 pm.

stories.title: Karnataka releases 1st PUC exam schedule for 2027
stories.summary: The Karnataka School Examination and Assessment Board has released the timetable for the 2027 1st Pre-University Course examinations. Exams are scheduled to begin on February 10 and conclude on February 23. The assessments will be conducted in an offline, pen-and-paper format for all affiliated institutions.

stories.title: SSC releases exam city slips for 2026 sub-inspector candidates
stories.summary: The Staff Selection Commission has released the exam city slips for the 2025 Paper-II examination for sub-inspectors in Delhi Police and Central Armed Police Forces. Candidates can download their slips and view their admission certificates by logging into the official commission website.

stories.title: CLAT 2027 admit cards expected soon
stories.summary: The Consortium of National Law Universities is expected to release admit cards for the CLAT 2027 entrance examinations shortly. Registered candidates will be able to access their hall tickets via the consortium website using their mobile number and password. The examination is scheduled for December 6, 2026.

stories.title: JEE Main 2027 registration deadline approaches
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency will close registration for the JEE Main 2027 Session 1 on November 22. While 10.47 million applications have been received, only 8.38 million candidates have completed the fee payment process. A late fee window will be available for those who miss the initial deadline.

stories.title: HPBOSE releases admit cards for November 2026 TET
stories.summary: The Himachal Pradesh Board of School Education has released admit cards for the TGT Arts and JBT Teacher Eligibility Test. The exams are scheduled for November 22 at centres across the state. Applicants require their application number and date of birth to download the necessary documentation.

stories.title: Haryana announces December 2026 HTET exam dates
stories.summary: The Board of School Education, Haryana has scheduled the 2026 Teacher Eligibility Test for December 26 and 27. Level III exams will take place on December 26, with Levels I and II following on December 27. The board has also introduced new rules for candidates this year.

stories.title: NEET SS 2026 registration closes today
stories.summary: The National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences closes registration for NEET SS 2026 today, November 18. The examination is scheduled for December 2026. Candidates may access the application portal at nbe.edu.in. The correction window opens on November 20, with exam city slips available from November 30.

stories.title: International student applications show rebound
stories.summary: The number of international students applying to US colleges via the Common App is up 9 percent this year, according to new data. This follows a decrease of the same proportion between the 2024 to 25 and 2025 to 26 academic years, returning to a post-pandemic upward trajectory.

stories.title: Philippines opens medical exams to Indian graduates
stories.summary: Indian medical graduates from recognised institutions in the Philippines may now sit for the country's Physician Licensure Examination. The decision, confirmed by Indian Ambassador Harsh Kumar Jain, allows graduates to obtain registration to practise medicine, establishing a pathway for reciprocal medical licensing arrangements between the two nations.

stories.title: UK student visa applications fall by 20 percent
stories.summary: UK student visa applications fell to 349,900 by the end of October 2026, a 20 percent decline compared to the same period last year. Dependant applications also dropped by 32 percent. The Home Office attributes the trend to increasingly restrictive immigration policies affecting international student arrivals.

stories.title: UK student visa applications drop 31 percent
stories.summary: Sponsored study visa applications in the UK fell 31 percent in October 2026 compared to the same month last year, with 5,800 applications recorded. Universities are currently preparing for a proposed 925 pound annual levy on international students set to take effect from August 2028.

stories.title: Indian graduate enrolments in US decline
stories.summary: The Open Doors 2026 report shows Indian graduate student enrolments in the US fell 34.4 percent, while participation in Optional Practical Training rose 26.8 percent. Despite the shift in composition, India remains the largest source of international students, with 339,435 students during the 2025 to 26 year.

stories.title: Visa refusals cause losses for Irish universities
stories.summary: Four Irish universities expect to lose over 8 million euro in tuition fees for the 2026 to 27 academic year due to international student visa refusals. The losses have raised concerns regarding the viability of postgraduate programmes that rely heavily on international student enrolments.

stories.title: Federal court strikes down fixed visa stay limits
stories.summary: A federal district court in Massachusetts has ruled against Department of Homeland Security regulations that sought to impose fixed stay limits on F, J and I visas. Judge Dennis Saylor found the policy violated the Administrative Procedure Act and contradicted the original intent of Congress.

stories.title: Court halts CPT internship restrictions
stories.summary: A federal court in Boston has temporarily blocked the Department of Homeland Security from enforcing stricter rules on Curricular Practical Training. The interim order provides relief to international students who rely on work-based learning, though the court has not yet issued a final verdict on the restrictions.

stories.title: New Zealand introduces short-term graduate visa
stories.summary: New Zealand has launched a six-month Short-Term Graduate Work Visa for international students who do not qualify for the standard Post-Study Work Visa. Available since November 16, 2026, the permit allows graduates to work for any employer while seeking long-term employment opportunities in the country.

stories.title: Google expands Gemini task automation
stories.summary: Google has updated its Gemini AI assistant to include task-completion capabilities for users in six countries, including India. Powered by the Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, the feature allows for multi-step automation of appointments, shopping and calendar management. Advanced features like automated phone calls remain restricted.

stories.title: Microsoft unveils new coding and cybersecurity AI models
stories.summary: Microsoft has introduced MAI Code 2, MAI Code 2 Flash and MAI Cyber 2 Flash, a suite of AI models for software development and security. The company claims these models offer performance comparable to leading systems at lower costs, reducing reliance on external AI developers.

stories.title: Senator demands Google disable AI in schools
stories.summary: US Senator Edward J. Markey has requested that Google allow K-12 schools to disable AI features like Gemini and AI Overviews without losing access to Google Search. He has given the company until November 30 to respond regarding student data safety and the impact on learning.

stories.title: Anthropic extends free AI access for teachers
stories.summary: Anthropic will provide free access to its Claude for Teachers service until July 30, 2028. The extension follows an agreement with teachers' unions regarding AI safety and student data privacy, allowing educators to use premium tools for lesson planning and curriculum development without a subscription fee.

stories.title: Students win hackathon with AI interview app
stories.summary: Two Benedictine University students won first place at the Hack the Nest competition for developing Interviewlenz. The application uses AI to provide feedback for technical coding interviews. The project was created by the students to address a perceived gap in how peers prepare for professional assessments.

stories.title: NeeevAI signs contracts with 26,000 schools
stories.summary: Ed-tech start-up NeeevAI reports it has signed contracts with 25,786 schools to introduce AI as a subject from Class 1 to 12. The company claims to have trained 2 lakh teachers and expects to reach 3.1 million students by April 2027.

stories.title: India adopts AI in schools without public debate
stories.summary: The Indian Ministry of Education has partnered with OpenAI to provide ChatGPT to government school teachers, while Andhra Pradesh is piloting AI tutors. Unlike in the West, where some regions have paused AI integration, these implementations are proceeding through procurement deals rather than public policy debate.

stories.title: AI tutoring proposed as classroom supplement in Korea
stories.summary: AI tutoring could provide speaking practice for students unable to afford private academies, according to a recent report. While the technology may reinforce vocabulary and grammar, the author notes that AI feedback remains unreliable and young learners still require consistent supervision from parents and teachers.

stories.title: CISCE launches nationwide digital assessment for students
stories.summary: The Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations has launched SHINE 2026, a digital assessment tool to identify learning gaps. Nearly 450 schools participated within 48 hours, generating over three million student responses. The initiative aims to strengthen classroom teaching through targeted data-driven interventions.

stories.title: Bodhan AI partners to train one million teachers
stories.summary: Bodhan AI has partnered with three education groups to train over one million teachers in AI literacy over the next 18 months. The programme aims to assist educators with lesson planning, content creation, and administrative tasks. The initiative is supported by the Learning Links Foundation and Vidya Shakti.

stories.title: CBSE mandates mentor enrolment for teachers
stories.summary: The Central Board of Secondary Education has directed its 33,287 affiliated schools to enrol experienced teachers as mentors under the MITRA initiative. The programme aims to provide personalised support to in-service teachers to help them become reflective practitioners. Principals must facilitate the registration of eligible staff.

stories.title: U.S. Department of Education awards UNF $2.6M to help math teachers use AI - Florida Politics
Arcadia middle school tests AI classroom tool
stories.summary: Arcadia Middle School is testing a UW-Madison AI tool that records and transcribes group discussions in real time. The software allows teachers to filter conversations for keywords to monitor student participation and concept mastery. The teacher noted that tracking every student conversation manually is physically impossible.

stories.title: Armenia launches AI portal for teachers
stories.summary: Armenia’s National Center for Educational Technologies has launched an AI portal featuring 65 tools grouped by educational objective. The site provides over 100 prompt examples aligned with the national curriculum. The selection process for the tools is based on principles of ethics and learner safety.

stories.title: CBSE issues mentor enrolment details for MITRA
stories.summary: The Central Board of Secondary Education has requested that principals register three to five teachers on the National Mission for Mentoring portal. The MITRA initiative, led by the National Council for Teacher Education, seeks to build a national network of experienced educators to guide in-service staff.

stories.title: CBSE Asks Schools To Enrol 3-5 Experienced Teachers As Mentors Under MITRA Initiative - News18
Oakridge Bengaluru principal shortlisted for global award
stories.summary: Kavita Sukhani of Oakridge International School Bengaluru has been shortlisted for Principal of the Year at the Tes Awards for International Schools 2026. She is the only nominee from India among eight global finalists. The awards recognise leadership and contributions to international education.

stories.title: Delhi teachers may receive special leave for census duty
stories.summary: The Directorate of Census Operations has proposed 15 days of special leave for teachers deployed as enumerators and supervisors for Census 2027. Approximately 60,000 government officials were involved in the exercise, which took place during summer vacations. The proposal is currently under consideration by the Delhi government.

stories.title: Nigeria sets 2027 deadline for teacher licensing
stories.summary: The Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria has announced that all teachers must obtain professional certification and licences by the end of 2027. The council warned that teaching without these credentials will no longer be tolerated. The mandate applies to all educators regardless of their current status.

stories.title: South African study highlights principal role in teacher development
stories.summary: A study suggests that school principals are essential for motivating teachers to pursue professional development. Many educators currently view such training as an unnecessary burden alongside overcrowded classrooms and heavy workloads. Empowered teachers are identified as the primary starting point for improving quality education.

stories.title: Morris school districts to host 2027 AI summit
stories.summary: The Morris School District and Morris Plains School District are seeking presenters for an upcoming Artificial Intelligence summit. The event is scheduled to take place on February 16, 2027, at Morristown High School.

stories.title: BOTEPCO and UNICEF reach 564 schools
stories.summary: The Botswana Technical Education Programme and UNICEF have engaged over 7,000 teachers across 564 schools. The initiative focuses on educational outreach and professional support for staff within the region.

stories.title: Nigeria mandates professional licences for teachers by 2027
stories.summary: The Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria has set a December 2027 deadline for all teachers to obtain professional certification. The council stated it is intensifying efforts to enforce standards through compulsory examinations. Practitioners without the required credentials will not receive official recognition from the council.

stories.title: J&K to reserve 25 percent of private school seats
stories.summary: Jammu and Kashmir will implement a 25 percent reservation for students from economically weaker sections and disadvantaged groups in private schools. The initiative follows Section 12(1)(c) of the Right to Education Act. The government aims to promote equitable access to schooling across the Union Territory.

stories.title: India targets 75,000 new medical seats by 2029
stories.summary: Health Minister JP Nadda announced a target to add 75,000 medical seats by 2029. The number of medical colleges in India has grown from 387 to 863 over the past decade. The government continues to focus on expanding medical education infrastructure and training capacity.

stories.title: UP Cabinet approves Rs 281 crore Deep Tech U-Hub at IIT Kanpur
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Cabinet approved the construction of a Deep Tech U-Hub at the IIT Kanpur Noida campus. The project will cost Rs 281.03 crore and is targeted for completion within 24 months. The state has allocated Rs 100 crore for the initiative in the 2026-27 budget.

stories.title: Keralam launches Kudumbashree campus initiative for students
stories.summary: Keralam's all-women network Kudumbashree has launched an initiative to help female college students earn income and develop entrepreneurial skills alongside their studies. Local Self-Government Minister K M Shaji inaugurated the project at Kozhikode beach, stating the organisation would guide young people in realising their aspirations.

stories.title: Shoolini and Edinburgh partner on engineering degrees
stories.summary: Shoolini University is partnering with the University of Edinburgh to offer engineering degrees with study in India and Scotland. The program uses a 2+2 or 2+3 model. Shoolini plans to subsidise the costs through its other programs, viewing the partnership as an investment in academic development.

stories.title: G Kishan Reddy to pay exam fees for 4,741 students in Secunderabad
stories.summary: Union Minister G Kishan Reddy will pay the Telangana SSC Board examination fees for 4,741 Class 10 students across 87 government schools in his constituency. The initiative is intended to support students in their education and follows similar efforts undertaken by the minister in previous years.

stories.title: Maharashtra NEET UG 2026-27 fills 99.56 percent of seats
stories.summary: Maharashtra has filled 11,431 of its 11,481 available MBBS and BDS seats for the 2026-27 academic year. Following nine rounds of counselling, 50 seats remain vacant. Government colleges reached full occupancy, while private institutions accounted for the remaining openings.

stories.title: Tripura college receives NCTE approval for integrated BEd course
stories.summary: Dharmanagar Government Degree College is the first in Tripura to receive approval for a four-year integrated BEd programme under NEP-2020. The state higher education department intends for other general degree colleges to follow suit as they transition into multidisciplinary institutions.

stories.title: CBSE curriculum changes cause uncertainty for schools
stories.summary: The CBSE has introduced multiple curriculum updates for Classes 6 to 9 during the 2026-27 academic year, including shifts in language and AI requirements. The frequent revisions have complicated academic planning for principals and required schools to repeatedly adjust their teaching schedules and staff roles.

research.title: What Majority Labels Hide: Annotator Disagreement and Model Errors in Multi-Dialect Arabic Sexism Detection
research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: Judgements of sexism are subjective and may vary across communities, yet sexism detection datasets usually reduce annotator judgements to a single majority label, obscuring disagreement and how models behave on contested cases. We introduce MuDAS, a. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Autistic brains look surprisingly similar on average. Then scientists looked closer.
research.summary: Scientists discovered that although people with and without autism show surprisingly similar average brain activity, individuals with autism exhibit much greater differences from one another, especially in regions involved in social understanding. The findings suggest that traditional research methods may be overlooking crucial differences that could help unlock.
